why: Build the tree from the edge list (parent -> children, child -> parent), validate it in priority order (format, duplicate edge, more than two children, several roots, cycle), then print it with a preorder traversal that wraps every subtree in parentheses.
hints: Separate the work into parse, validate, print. Checks run in priority order E1 to E5, and the first that fails decides the answer.

Track a set of seen pairs (E2), the child list of each parent (E3: a third child), and which nodes have a parent. Roots are nodes with no parent: more than one is E4; none, or a root that cannot reach every node, means a cycle (E5).
Print recursively: S(v) = '(' + v + S(first child) + S(second child) + ')', children sorted alphabetically. Labels are single letters, so at most 26 nodes; parsing the string is the O(length) part.
pitfalls: Any malformed token, such as a missing parenthesis, extra space or lowercase label, is E1 and beats all other errors.
Report the highest-priority error, even if a lower one appears earlier in the string.
With zero roots everything is in a cycle: report E5, not E4.
statement:
You are given a string pairs of parent-child pairs separated by single spaces. Each pair is written (A,B) with uppercase letters, meaning A is the parent of B.

If the pairs form a valid binary tree, return its S-expression. Otherwise return the highest-priority error code that applies:

  • E1: the string is malformed (a token is not exactly (X,Y)).
  • E2: the same pair appears more than once.
  • E3: some parent has more than two children.
  • E4: there is more than one root (node with no parent).
  • E5: there is a cycle.

The S-expression of a node is ( + its label + the S-expressions of its children + ), with no spaces. When a node has two children, the alphabetically smaller label comes first.

Worked example. "(A,B) (B,C) (A,D)"

  • All tokens are well formed, no pair repeats, A has two children (B, D), B has one (C).
  • A has no parent, every other node has one, so A is the only root and there is no cycle.
  • S(C) = (C), S(B) = (B(C)), S(D) = (D).
  • S(A) = (A(B(C))(D)).

For "(A,B) (A,B)" the pair repeats, so the answer is E2.
